note: Ask one question at a time, in order. Each question maps to a manifest path, carries the pillar it serves, and tells the interviewer how to recommend an answer.

questions.ask: What shape is the workload: web (request and response), events (queue or schedule driven), worker (long-running consumer) or batch (run to completion)?
questions.recommend: web and events fit Lambda; worker and batch usually fit ecs-fargate. Pick the simplest runtime that meets the limits in Q2.

questions.ask: Which single port does the app listen on (web and worker only)?
questions.recommend: 8080: one port, as in the app contract.

questions.ask: Which path answers the health check? (The app also needs /version with the commit SHA and image digest.)
questions.recommend: /health.

questions.ask: What is the longest request or job, in seconds?
questions.recommend: Under 29 s keeps HTTP API and Lambda viable (V09); over 900 s rules Lambda out (V08).

questions.ask: What is the largest request or response payload, in whole MB?
questions.recommend: Over 6 MB rules Lambda out (V08); use presigned S3 uploads to stay on Lambda.

questions.ask: Does the app need a GPU, OS-level access or a licensed product?
questions.recommend: Any of these rules Lambda out; choose ecs-fargate (os, licence) or ec2-asg (gpu).

questions.ask: Is traffic steady, spiky or mostly idle?
questions.recommend: Spiky or idle: lambda-web (scale to zero, SUS02-BP01). Steady and high: ecs-fargate.

questions.ask: What is the expected peak requests per second and the latency target?
questions.recommend: Under a few hundred RPS with a relaxed latency target fits Lambda; tight p99 targets favour ecs-fargate.

questions.ask: Is the app public or internal, and is it abuse-prone?
questions.recommend: Lambda: http-api (throttle as cost ceiling); function-url when budget-first; cloudfront with WAF only when public and abuse-prone. ECS and EC2: alb.

questions.ask: Which skills does the team have: Kubernetes, containers, serverless?
questions.recommend: Match the runtime to existing skills. Choose eks-workload only with Kubernetes skills and a shared cluster.

questions.ask: How much on-call capacity does the team have?
questions.recommend: Little capacity: managed and serverless runtimes, alarm-based automatic rollback.

questions.ask: How much release risk can the product tolerate?
questions.recommend: Low tolerance: canary or linear with rollback: alarm. High tolerance: all-at-once.

questions.ask: Which release strategy per env: all-at-once, rolling, canary, linear or blue-green?
questions.recommend: dev: all-at-once or canary. prod: canary with rollback: alarm, steps rising to 100 and bake_minutes >= 1 (V01, V02). Check the compatibility matrix per runtime.

questions.ask: What recovery time (RTO) and recovery point (RPO) objectives, in minutes?
questions.recommend: RTO of 240 and RPO of 1440 suit backup-restore for a small product (V13 warns on optimistic values).

questions.ask: Which DR strategy: backup-restore, pilot-light, warm-standby or multi-site?
questions.recommend: backup-restore unless RTO is under 60 minutes; warm-standby and multi-site need a budget of at least 100 USD (V14).

questions.ask: Which environments are needed?
questions.recommend: dev and prod; one account per env (SEC01-BP01). prod needs promote_from: dev (V11).

questions.ask: What account label does each env use (a label such as dev or prod, never an account ID)?
questions.recommend: The env name. The label maps to an ID in the project repo's GitHub environment variables, never in the manifest (V10).

questions.ask: What is the data classification: public, internal, confidential or regulated?
questions.recommend: internal unless real user data is stored.

questions.ask: Is a customer-managed KMS key required?
questions.recommend: false (AES256 default) unless a compliance rule demands it.

questions.ask: Which AWS region for each env?
questions.recommend: The region nearest the users that offers every needed service; fewer regions means less cost and carbon (SUS).

questions.ask: What is the monthly cost ceiling in USD for the whole project?
questions.recommend: An ALB adds a fixed monthly cost: V06 warns under 40 USD; EKS needs at least 100 USD (V15).

questions.ask: Which pricing model: on demand, Spot in dev, Savings Plans for steady prod?
questions.recommend: Spot in dev only; a Savings Plan only once steady prod spend is known. Never scale_to_zero or Spot on prod (V16).

questions.ask: Which CPU architecture?
questions.recommend: arm64 for new apps (cheaper and less energy, SUS05-BP02); x86_64 only if a dependency lacks arm64.

questions.ask: Which CI provider: GitHub Actions or CodePipeline?
questions.recommend: github-actions: OIDC with no long-lived keys and reusable workflows. CodePipeline is not built yet (V17).

questions.ask: Does the app use a database, and which kind?
questions.recommend: none or dynamodb for serverless; postgres when relational features are needed.

questions.ask: How are schema changes made?
questions.recommend: expand-contract: required whenever a strategy runs two versions at once (V12).

questions.ask: Which of the 7 Rs applies: rehost, replatform, refactor, retire, retain, relocate or repurchase?
questions.recommend: Rehost maps to ec2-asg, replatform to ecs-fargate, refactor to lambda-* or ecs-fargate. Retire, retain, relocate and repurchase end the intake with a note.
